A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SmartRAG work. All 22 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA experiments, component ablations, retrieval analyses and TriviaQA transfer results, including Tables 1, 4 and 8.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, transfer results and a query-generator ablation in Tables 1, 6 and 9.

M1.justification: The policy architecture, action sequence, warm-up construction, reward and PPO optimization remain unchanged. V2 clarifies that the retrieval quota and penalty can be disabled in suitable applications; the reported main configuration remains unchanged. The alternative warm-up query generator is an ablation.

E1.justification: Transfer evaluation expands from TriviaQA alone in v1 Appendix B.3 to TriviaQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue in v2 Section 4.5. This substantially broadens held-out question coverage. Appendix A.1 explicitly says the added multihop datasets are evaluated as single-step tasks; the earlier dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds Self-RAG, SKR and GPT4 Rewriter + SKR to Table 1's Llama2-7B comparison. Figure 2 also adds Self-RAG and GPT4 Rewriter + SKR. SKR already appeared in other v1 experiments, but its participation in Table 1 is new. These additions substantially strengthen comparison with separately trained adaptive retrieval systems.

E3.justification: The new query-generator ablation replaces GPT-3.5 with Llama2-7B for warm-up query generation while holding other settings fixed. The added transfer benchmarks use single-step testing. Existing training budgets, retrieval settings, backbone models and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix B.3 adds a controlled test of sensitivity to the warm-up query generator, and the existing transfer analysis gains evidence from two additional datasets. TriviaQA answerability stratification was already described in v1; v2 supplies its numerical retrieval rates. Earlier component, initialization, retrieval-number and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's statement that query-generator performance does not change significantly introduces no statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical table entries, including TriviaQA scores, are retained. V2 adds baseline results, query-generator results and transfer scores: SmartRAG achieves EM/F1 of 23.55/29.26 on 2WikiMultiHopQA and 4.84/13.33 on MuSiQue. It also reports TriviaQA category retrieval rates of 10.59%, 42.59% and 29.04%. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(6) and the underlying mathematical formulation are unchanged. New Appendix A.4 illustrates the existing discounted reward with two-trajectory examples; it introduces no new formal definitions, assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: jointly optimizing retrieval decisions, query rewriting and answer generation improves performance relative to separately optimized modules. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 interprets query-generator sensitivity as dependence on RL initialization, qualified by generator quality. Appendix A.5 adds a discussion of inference savings versus additional RL training effort, without timing measurements. The existing database-awareness interpretation is retained and elaborated.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies a 0.5 retrieval threshold for the previously described TriviaQA category analysis and documents the alternative query-generation setup and single-step treatment of the added datasets. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts and code-availability statement remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 supplies no measured latency or training time.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ho et al. (2020) and Trivedi et al. (2022) for the new transfer datasets and expands discussion of already cited Self-RAG and SKR. Consolidating the duplicate Wang et al. (2023) references does not remove a distinct work. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 creates a dedicated joint-optimization results subsection, moves and expands dataset transfer from Appendix B.3 to Section 4.5, and adds reward, cost and query-generator explanations. It also updates the publication header and affiliation. These are targeted expansions and reorganizations; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 1 and Figure 2, relocates and expands v1's transfer Table 8 as Table 6, and adds query-generator Table 9. It also adjusts table formatting and figure placement. Most existing figures and tables retain their displays and content.

improvement.justification: The added GPT4 Rewriter + SKR comparison more directly tests the central joint-optimization argument, while transfer and query-generator experiments strengthen its empirical support. Explicit TriviaQA retrieval rates repair a reporting gap in v1. These benefits outweigh limited problems in the additions: restricted single-step transfer testing, efficiency claims without timing measurements, and missing values in Appendix A.4's reward explanation.
